tasks.short: Keep pension, insurance and savings cover correct with brokers and carriers.

today.trigger: A joiner, leaver, hours change or life event, a monthly premium invoice, or a question from a fund, insurer or broker.
steps: Check in AFAS which CAO and which plan apply: industry pension for transport staff, the warehouse CAO plan, or a boven-CAO arrangement.
Send joiners, leavers and life events that the payroll file does not already carry to the broker or carrier.
Match premium invoices in accounts payable to headcount, wage components and the last pay run.
Answer the employee or the HR Administrator on accrual, cover or a rejected change.
Chase mismatches the fund or insurer returns and correct the source record.
systems: AFAS Profit (employee, contract, payroll, accounts payable)
Staffing agency portals (to see who is employed by an agency and stays off company plans)
drudgery: Retyping joiner and leaver lists that already sit in AFAS
Ticking premium spreadsheets against the pay run
Filing carrier PDFs and chasing the same mismatch twice
today.time_sinks: Waiting on brokers and funds, and reconciling figures that disagree with payroll, takes most of the elapsed time.

lenses.faster: The standard joiner, leaver and hours-change list is built from AFAS each day, so retyping and the first invoice match drop out. The specialist handles the break in the rule and the call with the broker.
lenses.autonomous: A contract change in AFAS opens a plan checklist the same day and adds clear cases to the monthly carrier batch. A case that breaks a written rule waits on the exception list.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort the company would keep every employee and every leaver visibly correct on pension and insured benefits, and would review cover against the CAOs each year.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses the retyping and the invoice ticking. The part people value, fixing a real pension or insurance problem for a colleague, stays.
lenses.options: For a disputed case the specialist can put the fund's reading, the CAO reading and the employer cost of each side by side before calling the broker.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the eligibility rules and the exception log that payroll and the carriers run on, and reviews the breaks each week.
reach: Payroll Specialist: clear pension-file mismatches before month-end
Bookkeeper: explain a benefit premium invoice before it is paid
HR Administrator: complete a standard joiner's plan enrolment from the checklist

tasks.human_edge: Judgement when a life event, a long sickness or a partial contract does not fit the written rule, and the relationship with the broker and the fund.
tasks.pattern_why: Eligibility is a set of written rules on AFAS records, and the monthly carrier batch can be prepared from those records. Outgoing messages and any write-off of a mismatch still need approval because a wrong pension or insurance record is hard to unwind.

in_practice.trigger: An AFAS contract event, the monthly premium invoice, or a carrier rejection.
steps: Build the day's joiner, leaver and change list from AFAS, split by transport CAO, warehouse CAO and boven-CAO.
Apply the written plan rules and separate clear cases from exceptions.
Draft the carrier batch and the invoice match, with each mismatch linked to a person and a pay period.
Specialist approves the batch and works the exception queue with the broker or Payroll.
File the approval and the carrier response on the employee and on the plan log.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves each outgoing batch and every exception before a carrier is told to change cover or a premium difference is accepted.
data_needed: Plan rules and eligibility per CAO
AFAS contract, hours and wage components
Premium invoices and carrier rejection codes
Who is a flex worker on an agency contract
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list 'Plan changes' and a note on the AFAS employee.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit already holds the contract, hours and wage components that Dutch pension and insurer reporting is built from.
Professional goods transport under CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer is tied to the industry pension fund BPF Vervoer, with monthly data coming from payroll.
The collective discount on basic Dutch health insurance has ended; any remaining collective cover is on supplementary insurance and must be checked before it is administered as a current plan.

risks: A second list of enrolments that drifts from AFAS will send the wrong people to the fund.
Pension and health data are personal data under the AVG; life-event notes need a narrow audience.
Warehouse staff and transport staff may sit in different plans, and one shared rule will mis-enrol people.
Flex workers usually stay on the agency's pension, and adding them to the company plan creates a false entitlement.
research_questions: What share of these hours is broker and fund contact, and what share is retyping mutations AFAS payroll already sends?
Which plans does Noordhaven actually sponsor for each CAO, and which eligibility rules are written down?
How many carrier rejections arrive in a month, and are the reasons coded or only in email?
Do any flex workers appear on company pension or insurance, or is that entirely with the three agencies?

tasks.short: Grade a job into the right function group and CAO salary scale.

today.trigger: A new role, a changed warehouse or transport job, a hire that does not fit an existing function, or a manager who disputes a grade.
steps: Read the request and the current functieomschrijving, if one exists.
Compare the work with reference functions in the transport CAO or the warehouse CAO.
Look up similar jobs in AFAS across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
Propose a functiegroep, scale and whether the role stays in the CAO or goes boven-CAO.
Explain the grade to the manager and hand the agreed scale to Payroll and the Recruiter.
systems: Recruitee (the vacancy this grade will support)
drudgery: Searching old files for the last similar job
Copying scale amounts into a mail by hand
Rewriting the same comparison for each site
today.time_sinks: Finding a reliable reference function and reconstructing how the last similar job was graded.

lenses.faster: The pack of similar jobs, CAO references and current scale amounts is ready before the specialist starts, so the hunt through files drops out. The grading conversation with the manager stays.
lenses.autonomous: A request for a new or changed function assembles similar AFAS jobs, the relevant CAO references and the scale difference by site.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every role, including seasonal warehouse roles filled by flex workers, would have a current grade and a recorded reason.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses hunting the last spreadsheet. Talking with a warehouse manager about what the job actually is remains the useful part.
lenses.options: For a borderline job, show the two nearest reference functions and the scale, periodiek and allowance difference at each site.
lenses.altitude: The specialist maintains the function house and the reference jobs, and checks new grades against that house.
reach: Recruiter: a justified scale on the offer before it is sent in Recruitee
HR Business Partner: the grading pack for a reorganisation at one site
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: a function-group field in AFAS that reports can trust

tasks.human_edge: Seeing how the work is done on a shift, and signing a grade that the CAO, the manager and the works council can stand behind.
tasks.pattern_why: The comparison uses structured AFAS history plus unstructured CAO function text, and the proposed functiegroep is checkable against the published scales. Each grade changes someone's pay or an offer, so it counts only after approval.

in_practice.trigger: A manager or Recruiter asks for a grade, or a vacancy opens with no matching function in AFAS.
steps: Pull similar functions, scales and allowances from AFAS for the three sites.
Map the requested work to the closest CAO reference functions and to the company function house.
Draft the proposed functiegroep, scale step and CAO or boven-CAO status, with the pay difference.
Specialist decides, after the manager has confirmed the work.
Write the approved grade to AFAS and to the vacancy once consent rules are satisfied.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every grade before AFAS or Recruitee is updated. A change to the functiewaardering system itself goes to the works council for consent.
data_needed: Current function house and reference jobs
CAO function texts and wage scales for both CAOs
AFAS job, scale, FTE and site
The manager's description of the work
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint function-house log and the function record in AFAS.

evidence.claim: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer publishes function material and wage scales that a proposed grade can be checked against.
AFAS Profit stores function, scale and contract, so a proposal can be compared with jobs the company already pays.
Under the Works Councils Act, introducing or changing a job-evaluation or remuneration system requires works-council consent.

risks: Grading from a thin description will copy a past mistake into a new scale.
The US exempt and non-exempt test is the wrong frame; a CAO inschaling and a boven-CAO contract answer a different question.
A new grading aid can itself be a change to the functiewaardering system and need works-council consent.
Small teams at Venlo or Tilburg make a 'similar job' statistically thin.
research_questions: Is there a written functiewaardering with factors and reference jobs, or do people grade from memory?
How often is the real question CAO inschaling or boven-CAO, and how often is any exempt-style test used?
On ten recent grades, does the proposed functiegroep match the CAO function book when someone else redoes the check?
Will the works council treat a new grading aid as a system change that needs consent?

tasks.short: Review benefit and safety-related terms and recommend policy changes.

today.trigger: A CAO renewal, a broker proposal, a rise in verzuim, an OR question, or a policy that has not been looked at since the last round.
steps: Collect the current policy from SharePoint and the plan documents from the broker.
Compare terms with the two CAOs and with what payroll actually pays.
Read absence and headcount from the Power BI extract to see who is affected.
Draft a recommendation with cost and employee effect.
Discuss it with the HR Director and, where consent is required, prepare the OR paper.
drudgery: Collecting PDFs and old OR papers
Rebuilding the same comparison table for each policy
Copying headcount figures out of Power BI by hand
today.time_sinks: Reading long CAO and policy texts, and aligning them with what AFAS actually pays, takes the longest.

lenses.faster: The first comparison of policy, CAO text and current cost is drafted before the specialist reads it, so the PDF collection drops out. The recommendation and the OR discussion stay.
lenses.autonomous: A CAO renewal date or a scheduled policy review opens a pack: current text, who it covers, last year's cost and open OR decisions.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort the company would review total reward and the insured benefits every year, and would fix gaps in sick-pay top-up and safety-related allowances while they are small.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses chasing document versions. Deciding what is worth changing, and writing a recommendation the director can use, is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Each proposal comes as three options with employee impact, employer cost and whether the works council must consent.
lenses.altitude: The specialist keeps a benefit and policy register with a review date and the OR decision on each item, and works from that register.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: link a required certificate (forklift, VCA, food safety) to an allowance rule
HR Director: a works-council paper on a benefit change
Controller: the cost of a proposed insured benefit before it is offered

tasks.human_edge: Choosing which change is worth a works-council proposal, and standing behind that recommendation with the HR Director.
tasks.pattern_why: The sources are unstructured and the product is advice. The specialist remains responsible for what is recommended and for what is put to the works council.

in_practice.trigger: A review date, a CAO renewal, a broker proposal, or a question from the HR Director or the OR.
steps: Pull the current policy, the CAO clauses and the last OR decision from SharePoint.
Summarise who is covered and what AFAS and Power BI show it cost last year.
Draft three options, each with cost, employee effect and the consent route.
Specialist edits the recommendation and decides what goes forward.
File the decision and the next review date on the policy register.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist owns the recommendation. A change to pension, savings, remuneration or job evaluation is not offered to staff before the works council has consented.
data_needed: Current policies and broker plan summaries
Both CAO texts and the OR decision log
Headcount, absence and wage-component cost from the AFAS extract
Which certificates are tied to pay
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint policy register, with the OR decision linked.

evidence.claim: Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract already shows headcount and absence, which a benefits review needs for who is affected.
Pension, profit-sharing, savings, remuneration and job-evaluation rules fall under works-council consent before they are changed.
A model can summarise long CAO and policy texts into a comparison a specialist then checks against the source.

risks: A summary that misstates a CAO article will flow into an OR paper and then into pay.
Health and safety duties sit largely with site operations and the prevention officer; a benefits paper can overreach into the RI&E.
Cost figures from a nightly extract can lag a pay correction and overstate a saving.
Broker proposals are sales documents and need a check against claims history.
research_questions: Which benefit policies already have an OR decision on file, and where is that register?
Is the right comparison set the industry CAO, the warehouse CAO and a few peer arrangements the company may lawfully hold?
Does cheaper research lead the director to want an annual review, or do the CAOs fix most terms so policy change stays rare?
Which safety-related terms does this role own, and which sit with site operations and Learning and Development?

tasks.short: Advise managers and employees on CAO, pay, benefits and classification.

today.trigger: A manager or employee asks, by mail, Teams or on the floor, about a scale, an allowance, a periodiek, sick pay or a classification.
steps: Read the question and open the person's record in AFAS.
Find the article in the correct CAO or the company policy on SharePoint.
Check with Payroll when the question is about an amount already paid.
Answer the manager or employee and file the mail.
If the same question keeps returning, mention it to the HR Director.
drudgery: Searching the CAO PDF for an article used many times before
Rebuilding the same explanation of ploegentoeslag or reiskosten
Looking up scale step and FTE one person at a time
today.time_sinks: Interruptions through the day, and questions that arrive with too little fact to answer safely.

lenses.faster: Known questions arrive with the CAO article, the person's AFAS facts and a draft answer, so the search drops out. The specialist still checks and sends the answer.
lenses.autonomous: A mail that matches a known question creates a draft reply with the source attached. The specialist sends it.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every shift manager would get a reliable first answer on scale, allowances and sick-pay top-up, and repeated questions would become a short handbook.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses searching the same PDF. The valued part is a straight answer a manager can use with their team.
lenses.options: For anything ambiguous, draft a short answer, a stricter CAO reading, and the back-pay if the stricter reading is right.
lenses.altitude: The specialist publishes the stable answers and spends the week on questions that do not fit them.
reach: HR Business Partner: a first-line CAO pay answer for a shift manager
Recruiter: how scale and allowances look in the first year of an offer
Payroll Specialist: which article supports a wage component

tasks.human_edge: Giving an answer a manager or employee will trust, and carrying the liability when the reply is a promise about pay.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist stays the adviser. A draft grounded in the CAO and the employee record makes the reply faster, and a wrong written answer on wages creates back-pay.

in_practice.trigger: A question in Outlook or Teams from a manager, an employee or an HR colleague.
steps: Identify the person, the site, the CAO and the wage components already in AFAS.
Attach the matching CAO article or policy and draft the answer.
Flag when the question needs Payroll, the HR Business Partner or a formal complaint route.
Specialist edits and sends the answer.
If the question is new and stable, add it to the handbook.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist sends every answer that states an amount, a scale or an entitlement. Payroll checks anything that would change the next pay run.
data_needed: The question and the person's AFAS contract, scale, hours and site
The two CAO texts and the company handbook
Current allowance rules, including shift and travel
What the manager is allowed to see under the AVG arrangement
in_practice.logs_to: The sent mail in Outlook, plus a SharePoint entry when the answer sets a precedent.

evidence.claim: Managers already ask these questions in Outlook and Teams, so a draft can sit in the tool they use.
Dutch statutory sick pay is at least 70 percent for 104 weeks, and the CAO often tops that up; advice has to follow the CAO that covers the person.
Written pay advice that understates a CAO allowance creates a back-pay exposure and a works-council issue if the practice spreads.

risks: An answer on the wrong CAO, transport instead of warehouse, pays the wrong allowance.
Individual pay and verzuim details in a draft can be shown to a manager who should not see them.
A fluent draft will be forwarded unchanged and become an unofficial policy.
Advice that touches continued pay during illness can cut across a Wet verbetering poortwachter case owned by the HR Business Partner.
research_questions: What are the twenty most repeated questions, and are the answers stable in the CAO and the handbook?
How often is the first draft wrong when checked against ten real past cases?
Who may see this employee's pay and absence, under the current AVG rules agreed with the works council?
Which questions must stay with the HR Business Partner because they are about a person in a verzuim trajectory?

tasks.short: Design and run the merit, incentive and allowance programmes.

today.trigger: The annual cycle, a CAO one-off or periodiek round, a proposed warehouse allowance, or a manager asking for a bonus for boven-CAO staff.
steps: Confirm what the two CAOs already fix: scale, periodiek, ploegentoeslag and other allowances.
Design or update the company scheme for anything above that, usually boven-CAO merit or a site allowance.
Calculate who qualifies, using Excel on an AFAS extract, and handle part-time, sickness and mid-year joiners.
Have Payroll load the approved amounts as wage components.
Tell managers the outcome and file the scheme for the OR where consent applies.
drudgery: Rebuilding eligibility in Excel each cycle
Explaining the same exception rules for sickness and part-time
Copying approved amounts back into AFAS one group at a time
today.time_sinks: The calculation and the exception list, especially across three sites with different shift patterns, take the longest.

lenses.faster: Once the rules are written, the eligible population and the amounts are calculated from AFAS, and the manual workbook drops out. Design and the approval conversation stay.
lenses.autonomous: After a pay period closes, the approved scheme runs and posts an exception list for new hires, long-term sick and incomplete hours.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort the company would run a clear, published scheme for every company allowance and for boven-CAO merit, and would show each agency the inlenersbeloning elements for the roles it fills.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the workbook. Designing a scheme that shift teams experience as fair is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: For a proposed incentive, show payouts at low, expected and high volume, for full-time, part-time and a typical flex-covered shift.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the scheme rules inside AFAS and reviews outcomes once a cycle, including whether flex workers' inlenersbeloning still matches.
reach: Payroll Specialist: a new wage component specified so it can be loaded once
FP&A Analyst: bonus and allowance figures for the forecast
HR Administrator: the inlenersbeloning sheet for the three agencies

tasks.human_edge: Deciding the design, and whether the result is fair across shifts, sites, part-time staff and flex workers.
tasks.pattern_why: An approved scheme is a set of rules on payroll data and can be calculated and checked. Paying it changes wages, and a new or changed scheme needs a person and often the works council before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: The annual cycle, a CAO change, or a request for a new company allowance or boven-CAO merit round.
steps: Separate what the CAO already pays from what the company scheme decides.
Calculate eligibility and amounts from AFAS, with exceptions listed.
Draft the manager note and, for a scheme change, the OR consent paper.
Specialist and HR Director approve the amounts; Payroll loads them.
Compare the paid result with the approval and update the agency inlenersbeloning sheet.
in_practice.human_gate: No amount is loaded and no scheme text is issued until the specialist approves the batch. A new or changed remuneration rule goes to the works council first.
data_needed: Written scheme rules and both CAO texts
AFAS scale, hours, allowances, sickness and hire date by person
Manager inputs where the scheme uses a judgement score
Current agency orders and the pay elements that count as inlenersbeloning
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint scheme file and the wage-component batch in AFAS, with the approver and date.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit payroll can pay a wage component once the amount and the rule are explicit and approved.
A remuneration system needs works-council consent before it is introduced or changed.
Agency workers at a hirer are entitled to the hirer's inlenersbeloning, so company allowances and scales have to be communicable to the three agencies.

risks: A discretionary merit pot on top of a CAO that already has periodieken can double-pay or breach equal treatment.
Warehouse productivity pay can conflict with the CAO and with Arbeidstijdenwet rest rules if it rewards unsafe extra hours.
Manager scores fed into a formula can be an employment decision under the EU AI Act if the score is itself model-generated.
Flex parity drifts when a company allowance changes and the agencies are told late.
research_questions: How much of pay is fixed by the two CAOs, and how much is a company scheme that can be redesigned?
Are warehouse incentives in use today, and do they survive a check against the CAO?
Can AFAS calculate the approved components, with Payroll checking only the exception list?
What exactly must be sent to the three agencies so inlenersbeloning matches the own-employee package?

tasks.short: Judge classification and salary complaints and advise on the outcome.

today.trigger: An employee or manager disputes a functiegroep, a scale step, a missed periodiek or a difference with a colleague.
steps: Hear the complaint and collect the mail trail.
Pull the person's function, scale, periodieken and hours from AFAS.
Compare with colleagues in the same functiegroep and site, usually in Excel.
Read the CAO rule and any earlier promise.
Advise the manager and the employee on the outcome and the back-pay if the grade moves.
drudgery: Building the comparison sheet from scratch for every complaint
Anonymising colleague pay by hand
Searching mail for an old promise about the grade
today.time_sinks: Assembling a fair comparison set, and doing it again when the first set is the wrong CAO or the wrong site.

lenses.faster: The dossier arrives with scale history, the CAO clause and a comparison set, so building the spreadsheet drops out. The conversation and the decision stay.
lenses.autonomous: A complaint logged in Outlook or Teams opens a dossier from AFAS the same day. The specialist sends every answer.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every complaint would get a full, consistent dossier within a few days, and the company would see which functions generate the same dispute at more than one site.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the comparison sheet. Listening to the employee and explaining the outcome is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Show the outcome under the current grade, the requested grade and a middle step, each with back-pay and the effect on inlenersbeloning.
lenses.altitude: The specialist keeps the precedent list and the pay ranges, and the next complaint starts from that position.
reach: HR Business Partner: a prepared case before a difficult conversation at a site
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: the comparison set later used for pay-transparency reporting
HR Director: a flag when one complaint will set a precedent for all three sites

tasks.human_edge: Hearing the person and deciding the outcome, including when two people were graded differently for a reason the numbers do not show.
tasks.pattern_why: The dossier and the draft advice can be produced from AFAS, the CAO and prior cases, and another person can check the figures. The outcome affects a named employee and can become a precedent, so it counts only after the specialist decides.

in_practice.trigger: A written or verbal complaint about classification or pay.
steps: Open a case and pull function, scale history, hours, site and CAO from AFAS.
Build a comparison set that is large enough to use and small enough not to identify a colleague by accident.
Draft the advice with the three outcomes and the back-pay.
Specialist decides after speaking with the employee or the manager.
Record the precedent and, if pay changes, hand a checked amount to Payroll.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves every outcome before it is told to the employee or loaded into payroll. Cases that allege unequal treatment also go to the HR Director.
data_needed: The complaint and any earlier written promise
AFAS function, scale, periodiek, hours, site and CAO
A comparison group that does not identify colleagues
Prior precedents and the relevant CAO article
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint complaint log, the AFAS employee note, and the payroll instruction if the grade changes.

evidence.claim: Excel on an HR extract is already how compensation staff build a comparison set; the change is doing it from a fixed extract with a check.

The EU pay transparency directive, due to be transposed by 7 June 2026, gives employees rights to pay criteria and to pay-level information for comparable work, with care for groups small enough to identify someone.
Individual grading and pay decisions sit in the employment area of the EU AI Act, where a person should approve the outcome for the worker.

risks: A comparison set that is too small identifies a colleague and breaches the AVG.
A complete-looking draft will be forwarded as the decision before the specialist has heard the person.
Treating one site's exception as a rule creates back-pay at the other two sites.
A model-written outcome on an individual grade is an employment decision and needs a human on each case.
research_questions: How many classification and salary complaints arrive in a year, and what share is missing data?
Are comparison groups inside a site and functiegroep large enough to show a range without naming a colleague?
On ten closed cases, does today's advice match the CAO when someone else redoes the check?
Which complaints must go to the HR Business Partner or a formal complaints route agreed with the OR?

tasks.short: Write job descriptions, function groups and the salary scales.

today.trigger: A new job, a CAO wage-table update, a reorganisation, or a Recruiter who has no description to put on a vacancy.
steps: Interview the manager and look at a neighbouring function.
Draft the functieomschrijving in the company template on SharePoint.
Place it in a functiegroep and copy the scale from the CAO table into Excel and AFAS.
Have the manager confirm the text.
Give the approved text to the Recruiter and the scale to Payroll.
drudgery: Formatting the same template
Copying CAO wage amounts into AFAS and Excel
Chasing managers for a description that already exists in an old file
today.time_sinks: Getting a description that matches the work, and loading a full CAO scale change without missing a step or an allowance.

lenses.faster: The first description in the company template, and the scale difference when a CAO table changes, are ready to edit. Formatting and retyping the wage table drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A published CAO wage change lines the new amounts up against the current AFAS scales and lists every employee whose step would move.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every job that recruitment uses would have a current description, a functiegroep and a scale, shared by AFAS, Recruitee and the contract template.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting and retyping scales. Getting the work described so a new hire and a manager recognise it is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: For a new role, produce a tight description and a wider one, each mapped to a functiegroep and a scale, for the manager to choose from.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the function library and the scale table that recruitment, payroll and the agencies all use.
reach: Recruiter: a vacancy text in Recruitee drawn from the approved description
HR Administrator: the agreed scale in the SharePoint contract template
Learning and Development Specialist: the certificates the description requires, for Studytube

tasks.human_edge: Making the description true to the job and acceptable to the manager who will use it every time they hire.
tasks.pattern_why: Manager notes and CAO function text are unstructured. The output is a description in a fixed template plus a functiegroep and scale step that can be checked against the CAO wage table before anyone uses it.

in_practice.trigger: A request for a description, or a new CAO wage table.
steps: Turn the manager's notes into a draft in the company template, with tasks, certificates and site.
Propose the functiegroep and the scale from the CAO table and the function house.
On a wage-table update, list every AFAS scale row that changes and every employee it moves.
Specialist and the manager approve the description; the specialist approves the scale load.
Publish the approved text to SharePoint, AFAS and the Recruiter.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist approves each description and every scale change before it is loaded into AFAS or used in a vacancy or a contract. A change to the evaluation system also needs works-council consent.
data_needed: Manager notes and any existing description
CAO wage tables and function references for both CAOs
AFAS function and scale records
Certificate requirements used by Learning and Development
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint function library, with version and approver, and the scale table in AFAS.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit holds function and scale, so an approved CAO wage table can be loaded as structured steps and then checked.
A model can draft a job description from manager notes into a fixed template; the manager and the specialist still have to confirm that it matches the work.
Changing the job-evaluation system, as distinct from applying it to one job, requires works-council consent.

risks: A polished description that the manager has not checked will be wrong on certificates, shift pattern or the real tasks.
Loading a CAO table into the warehouse population, or the reverse, moves people onto the wrong scale.
Youth scales, allowances and part-time steps are easy to drop when a table is copied.
Descriptions written for recruitment drift from the text used to grade pay.
research_questions: Are current functieomschrijvingen on SharePoint complete, or behind the functions in AFAS?
Can the published CAO wage tables be read into scale steps, including youth scales and allowances, with a check that ties to the PDF?
Who must sign a description before recruitment or payroll uses it?
How many hours does a description take today from manager notes to the text on the vacancy?

tasks.short: Cost wage and CAO options for bargaining and management decisions.

today.trigger: A CAO round, a union proposal, the budget cycle, or the HR Director asking what a wage offer will cost.
steps: Pull headcount, scale, hours, allowances and employer charges from the AFAS extract.
Rebuild an Excel model by site, by CAO and for boven-CAO staff.
Add sickness, turnover, periodiek drift and the flex mix by hand.
Price the proposal and one or two variants.
Walk the HR Director and Finance through the result.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same pivot each round
Reconciling the workbook to payroll totals
Copying figures into a deck for the director
today.time_sinks: Getting a workbook that Finance will trust, and redoing it when the extract or the proposal changes.

lenses.faster: The model already ties to payroll, so rebuilding the workbook drops out. A new percentage is a rerun. Interpreting it and choosing what can be shared stay.
lenses.autonomous: When Finance opens the budget, or a written wage proposal arrives, the model recalculates from the latest nightly extract and files the scenario.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort every serious option in a CAO round would be costed by site and by CAO before anyone sat down, including the flex and sickness effects.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the pivot. Judging which scenario is realistic, with Finance in the room, is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: Price at least three paths: the claim as received, the industry-CAO path, and a company offer, each by site and by CAO.
lenses.altitude: The specialist owns the labour-cost model that HR and Finance both use, and improves the assumptions after each round.
reach: FP&A Analyst: labour-cost scenarios inside the budget cycle
Controller: a check that employer charges and the pay run tell the same story
HR Director: the employer cost of a union or OR proposal before a response goes out

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the assumptions, and deciding what management, the works council or the unions may see.
tasks.pattern_why: A wage-round cost is arithmetic on payroll data: headcount by scale step, hours, allowances and employer charges. The formulas can be coded, tied back to AFAS totals, and rerun with new percentages.

in_practice.trigger: A budget opening, a CAO proposal, or a request from the HR Director or the Controller.
steps: Refresh the model from the nightly AFAS extract, split by site, CAO and boven-CAO.
Apply the proposed percentages and the stated assumptions for sickness, turnover, periodiek drift and flex mix.
Reconcile the base to the last pay run and list populations the model cannot price.
Specialist reviews assumptions and releases the scenario to HR and Finance.
Store the scenario, the extract date and the audience it was shared with.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist sets the assumptions and approves any figure that leaves the HR and Finance circle. The model does not change a wage.
data_needed: Person-level scale, FTE, hours, allowances, overtime and employer charges
The proposal being costed
Assumptions for sickness, turnover, periodiek and flex volume
Last pay-run totals for the reconciliation
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint CAO cost library: scenario, extract date, assumptions, approver and audience.

evidence.claim: Power BI already reports on a nightly AFAS extract, which is the source a labour-cost model has to reconcile to.
Employer labour cost for bargaining is a calculation on headcount, scales, allowances and employer charges, and finance teams already do this in spreadsheets.
Bargaining figures are confidential, and sharing a scenario with the works council or a union is a management decision.

risks: A model that does not tie to the pay run will be rejected by the Controller at the moment it is needed.
Long-term sick, flex workers and boven-CAO contracts will be priced wrongly if they are forced into a CAO average.
Scenario files are sensitive; a SharePoint link sent too wide shows the bargaining position.
Nightly-extract lag around a payroll correction moves the cost of a one-off payment.
research_questions: Does the AFAS extract contain scale step, FTE, allowances, overtime and employer charges at person level for both CAOs?
Can a rebuilt model reproduce last year's wage cost within a tolerance Finance will accept?
Which assumptions move the result by more than one percent?
What may be shared with the works council or the unions, and what stays inside HR and Finance?

role.altitude: Owner of the pay and benefits system for Noordhaven: the function house, the wage components in AFAS, the carrier rules, and the labour-cost model. The specialist checks exceptions and handles the cases that need a person, including works-council consent and individual disputes.
reach: Payroll Specialist: prepare CAO scale loads and new wage components before the pay run
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: definitions of function group, scale and FTE in the nightly extract
Recruiter: the scale, allowances and description behind an offer in Recruitee
HR Business Partner: grading and CAO pay answers for a site manager
FP&A Analyst and Controller: labour-cost scenarios for the budget and for CAO rounds
HR Administrator: the salary clause in the contract template and the inlenersbeloning sheet for the agencies
Bookkeeper: a check of benefit premium invoices against headcount before payment
role.ceiling_note: One FTE cannot take the payroll month-end, the HR Director's relationship with the works council, or absence casework under the Wet verbetering poortwachter. Bargaining and consent calendars move slower than the analysis. Most of the 750 shift workers sit on standard CAO terms, so the volume is in clean rules and the value is in a smaller set of exceptions. Trust, back-pay liability and AVG limits cap how far advice on an individual person's pay can be handed to a system.
skills_to_grow: Writing eligibility and scheme rules so they can be tested against AFAS
Functiewaardering under both CAOs, including inlenersbeloning for agency staff
Pay transparency and equal treatment for a 1,200-person, three-site employer
Works-council proposals on pension, remuneration and job evaluation
Reading a labour-cost model and explaining it to Finance, the OR and union audiences
AVG practice for pay comparisons, especially small groups at one site
role.ambitious_version: With administration, drafting and costing handled, this role keeps a current function house and a total-reward picture for both CAOs and for boven-CAO staff, watches pay differences across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo through the year, and enters a CAO round or a works-council meeting with figures Finance will stand behind. Employees and the three agencies can see the scale, the allowances and the reason for the grade. The specialist's own time goes to disputed cases, scheme design and the relationship with the broker and the funds.
